subtopic: Nomenclature of Organic Compounds
stem:
Give the IUPAC names of the following compounds :
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CN}\)
(c) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)
(d) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{Br})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)
(e) \(\text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\)
(f) \(\text{Cl}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}\)
_note: FIGURE-DEPENDENT IN THE BOOK: parts (a)-(e) are printed as DRAWN BOND-LINE FORMULAS on page index 36 and only (f) is printed as text. Each drawing has been read off the page and written here as the equivalent condensed formula, which preserves the naming task. (a) is a three-carbon chain attached to a benzene ring; (c) is a seven-vertex zig-zag with a methyl on the 2nd and on the 5th vertex; (d) is a seven-vertex zig-zag whose 3rd vertex carries both Cl and Br.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
Classify the following reactions in one of the reaction type studied in this unit.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{HS}^{-} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{SH} + \text{Br}^{-}\)
(b) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{ClC}-\text{CH}_3\)
(c) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{HO}^{-} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Br}^{-}\)
(d) \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
_note: BOOK TYPO, corrected to the intended symbol per the transcription brief: in part (b) the printed page sets chlorine's lower-case l as a CAPITAL I, so the page reads "HCI" and "(CH3)2CIC". Verified at 22x against the genuine lower-case l in Ex 8.4(f) ("Cl2CHCH2OH"), whose glyph is an ascender with no top serif while the glyph here sits at cap height with serifs at both ends. Transcribed as Cl.

subtopic: Isomerism
stem:
What is the relationship between the members of following pairs of structures ? Are they structural or geometrical isomers or resonance contributors ?
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) and \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3\)
(b) A \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) in which the left carbon carries \(\text{D}\) above and \(\text{H}\) below while the right carbon carries \(\text{H}\) above and \(\text{D}\) below; and a \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) in which the left carbon carries \(\text{D}\) above and \(\text{H}\) below while the right carbon carries \(\text{D}\) above and \(\text{H}\) below.
(c) \(\text{H}-\text{C}(=\overset{+}{\text{O}}\text{H})-\text{OH}\) and \(\text{H}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{OH})-\text{OH}\)
_note: FIGURE-DEPENDENT IN THE BOOK: all three pairs are printed as DRAWN STRUCTURES on page index 37 and are described here from the page. In (a) the two bond-line drawings are a five-carbon chain with the C=O on the middle vertex, and a five-carbon chain with the C=O on the second vertex.

subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
stem:
For the following bond cleavages, use curved-arrows to show the electron flow and classify each as homolysis or heterolysis. Identify reactive intermediate produced as free radical, carbocation and carbanion.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{OCH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\dot{\text{O}} + \dot{\text{O}}\text{CH}_3\)
(b) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O} + {}^{-}\text{OH} \rightarrow {}^{-}\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\)
(c) \((\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Br} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}} + \text{Br}^{-}\)
(d) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{E}^{+} \rightarrow\) the cyclohexadienyl cation in which one ring carbon bears \(\text{E}\) and the ring carries a positive charge
_note: FIGURE-DEPENDENT IN THE BOOK: parts (b), (c) and (d) are printed as DRAWN bond-line structures on page index 37 (only (a) is printed as text). They have been read off the page and written as equations here; in (b) the ketone is drawn as a bond-line \(>\!\!=\!\text{O}\) (propan-2-one) and the product carries the minus sign on one of its methyl carbons.
